1//! Creating accessible PDF documents.
2//!
3//! # Introduction
4//!
5//! A document usually consists of many smaller semantic building blocks, like for example
6//! titles, headings, paragraphs, tables, headers, footers, and so on. However, it is important
7//! to understand that, by default, when exporting a document to PDF, all of this semantic
8//! information is lost.
9//!
10//! By default, a PDF document doesn't have a notion of a table or a
11//! paragraph. Instead, it consists of very low-level instructions, such as "draw
12//! a path at that location" or "draw a line of glyphs at that font size". A table is
13//! not encoded as a "table", but instead as a number of rectangle-like paths that happen
14//! to surround lines of text. This is what made PDF popular in the first place, as encoding
15//! information at such a low level allows to ensure a consistent viewing experience across
16//! different platforms and viewers.
17//!
18//! However, this design has drawbacks, one of the main ones being that it leads to the
19//! production of non-accessible documents. Especially in recent years, ensuring the
20//! accessibility of documents has become an increasingly important requirement.
21//! To address this deficiency, PDF introduced the notion of "tagged PDF", which consists
22//! of enriching PDF documents with additional semantic information in a way that can be
23//! interpreted by different consumers. krilla supports the creation of such documents.
24//!
25//! # A word on krilla's implementation
26//!
27//! As nearly everything in PDF, tagging is a really complex topic, and getting it right
28//! is very hard. Because of this, in line with the general philosophy of crate::third_party::krilla, some
29//! of the potential capabilities of tagged PDF are not directly supported. Instead, only
30//! a specific subset has been implemented, with a focus on features that improve the
31//! accessibility of documents.
32//!
33//! Please note that doing tagging 100% correctly as recommended by various PDF standards is very
34//! difficult. While the documentation lists many of the recommendations to abstract away
35//! as much as possible, users are still expected to consult the given specifications to
36//! ensure their implementation matches the specification. A "reference implementation" that
37//! could be good to consult is the [`typst-pdf`](https://github.com/typst/typst/tree/main/crates/typst-pdf)
38//! crate which implements most of the expected features for well-tagged PDFs.
39//!
40//! # Basic Principles
41//!
42//! The way tagged PDFs are created is by attaching a tag tree to the PDF document
43//! that encodes the logical structure of the document. As mentioned above, a raw PDF file
44//! mainly consists of text- and path-drawing primitives, which are not necessarily
45//! drawn in the logical reading order of the document. What the tag tree does is
46//! maping the different "snippets" of the PDF file to the tree-like structure in a way
47//! that reflects the logical structure of the document, in reading-order.
48//!
49//! For example, a document can consist of multiple "sections", where each section might contain
50//! headings, paragraphs or figures. A figure might consist of a table as well as a caption.
51//! A table consists yet again of smaller semantic components, like a header, footer
52//! and the data cells, which usually contain some text. These kinds of hierarchical structures
53//! can be encoded with the help of tagging.
54//!
55//! A tag tree consists of two components:
56//! - Group nodes, which represents a component with certain semantics. A group node must have
57//!   at least one child, otherwise it's discarded.
58//! - Leaf nodes, which represent the actual pieces on the page that form part of a group.
59//!
60//! # How to create a tagged document
61//!
62//! If you want to create a tagged document, you need to follow the following steps:
63//!
64//! 1) Ensure that you activate the `enable_tagging` attribute in [`SerializeSettings`].
65//! 2) Create a [tag tree](TagTree), which represents the "root" of a tag tree.
66//! 3) As you create your document, create new [tag groups](TagGroup) with corresponding [tags](Tag).
67//!    Nest them with other tag groups, if necessary, by using the `push` method.
68//! 4) Populate tag groups with [identifiers](Identifier), which represent the leaf nodes
69//!    in the tag tree. Identifiers are unique and point to a sequence of content on the
70//!    page. If you push an identifier to a tag group, then all content that is marked by
71//!    that identifier belongs semantically to that tag group. There are currently two ways
72//!    of obtaining an identifier:
73//!
74//!    - Use the `add_tagged_annotation` method on [`Page`], which allows you to associate
75//!      annotations to the content they correspond to. Currently, krilla only supports link
76//!      annotations, and a link annotation should always be a child in a tag group with the
77//!      [`TagKind`] [`Link`](TagKind::Link), with its sibling being an identifier or another tag group that is
78//!      to be associated with the link.
79//!    - Use the `start_tagged` command on [`Surface`], which returns an [Identifier], and
80//!      indicates that all content drawn on the surface should be associated with that
81//!      identifier, until you call the `end_tagged` method. *Important*: Note that you cannot
82//!      nest calls to `start_tagged`, and you have to ensure that you always call a corresponding
83//!      `end_tagged`. Otherwise, krilla will panic.
84//!
85//!      It is very important that each identifier you create has exactly one parent in the tag
86//!      tree. This means that you cannot create an identifier and not use it at all (0 parents),
87//!      or use the same identifier in two different parts of the tree (1+ parents). Otherwise,
88//!      export will fail.
89//!
90//! 5) Once you have built your tag tree, simply call `set_tag_tree` on [`Document`]. That's it!
91//!
92//! # Other notes
93//!
94//! Make sure that you carefully read the documentation of the other parts of this module, as
95//! there are some more points as well as best practices you need to keep in mind
96//! when creating well-tagged documents. The PDF specification is in some places very vague
97//! on how a tagged document should look like, so there is quite a bit of ambiguity.
98//!
99//! Apart from that, the PDF specification does make a few statements on requirements a well-tagged PDF
100//! should follows, although  those are not really "strict" requirements in the sense that they can
101//! be automatically checked by a PDF validator, so not conforming to some of those points does not
102//! suddenly make your document a badly-tagged document! However, if possible, you should still
103//! try to comply with the following requirements:
104//!
105//! - In general, all contents in your file should be tagged, either as an artifact or with
106//!   Span/Other.
107//! - The order of elements in the tag tree should represent the logical reading order, including
108//!   annotations.
109//! - Word breaks in text should be represented explicitly with spaces, instead of implicitly
110//!   by not including them, but instead positioning text in a way that "simulates" the spaces.
111//! - Hyphenation should be represented as a soft hyphen character (U+00AD) instead
112//!   of a hard hyphen (U+002D).
113//! - Tag groups should follow the best-practice of what kind of children they contain. See
114//!   [`TagKind`] for more information.
115//! - You should provide "Alt" descriptions for formulas and images.
116//! - In case you have a link annotation that applies to text that wraps into one or multiple
117//!   new lines, you should use the `quad_points` functionality to indicate the exact covered
118//!   areas of the link.
119//!
120//! Once again, the above is only a best-effort summary, if you are interested in creating
121//! completely well-tagged PDFs, you are advised to consult the given specifications.
122//!

152/// An artifact that should not be part of the accessible structure.
153#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Default)]
154pub struct Artifact {
155    /// The type of the artifact.
156    pub kind: ArtifactType,
157    /// The bounding box that incloses the artifact's visual content. Required
158    /// for background artifacts.
159    pub bbox: Option<Rect>,
160}
161
162impl Artifact {
163    /// Create a new artifact with a type and an optional BBox.
164    ///
165    /// You must provide a bounding box if `kind` is
166    /// [`ArtifactType::Background`] and you are targetting PDF 1.7, otherwise,
167    /// Krilla will later panic.
168    pub fn new(kind: ArtifactType, bbox: Option<Rect>) -> Self {
169        Self { kind, bbox }
170    }
171
172    /// Create a new artifact with a type and no bounding box.
173    pub fn with_kind(kind: ArtifactType) -> Self {
174        Self::new(kind, None)
175    }
176
177    /// Whether the artifacts requires a property list.
178    pub(crate) fn requires_properties(self, pdf_version: PdfVersion) -> bool {
179        self.bbox.is_some() || self.kind.map_pdf_version(pdf_version).to_pdf_artifact_type().is_some()
180    }
181
182    /// Whether the artifact requires a BBox.
183    pub(crate) fn requires_bbox(self, pdf_version: PdfVersion) -> bool {
184        // Background artifacts were introduced in PDF 1.7. In table 330, the
185        // standard makes bounding boxes mandatory for background artifacts
186        // only. PDF 2.0 lifts this requirement in table 363.
187        //
188        // When changing the below condition, also change the error at the
189        // callsite.
190        self.kind == ArtifactType::Background && pdf_version == PdfVersion::Pdf17
191    }
192}

194/// A type of artifact.
195#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Default)]
196pub enum ArtifactType {
197    /// The header of a page.
198    Header,
199    /// The footer of the page.
200    Footer,
201    /// For text in the back- or foreground of all pages.
202    Watermark,
203    /// Page numbers.
204    PageNumber,
205    /// Numbering artifacts before lines.
206    LineNumber,
207    /// Areas where there formerly was content, but which has been removed.
208    Redaction,
209    /// Bates numbering.
210    Bates,
211    /// Other artifacts arising from pagination not covered by the above variants.
212    PaginationOther,
213    /// Purely cosmetic typographical or design elements.
214    Layout,
215    /// Page artifacts, such as for example cut marks or color bars.
216    Page,
217    /// The background of a page or a graphical element.
218    Background,
219    /// Any other type of artifact.
220    #[default]
221    Other,
222}
223
224impl ArtifactType {
225    pub(crate) fn map_pdf_version(self, version: PdfVersion) -> Self {
226        match self {
227            Self::PageNumber | Self::LineNumber | Self::Redaction | Self::Bates if version < PdfVersion::Pdf20 => ArtifactType::PaginationOther,
228            Self::Header | Self::Footer | Self::Watermark if version < PdfVersion::Pdf17 => ArtifactType::PaginationOther,
229            Self::Background if version < PdfVersion::Pdf17 => ArtifactType::Other,
230            _ => self,
231        }
232    }
233
234    pub(crate) fn to_pdf_artifact_type(self) -> Option<pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType> {
235        match self {
236            ArtifactType::Header => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
237            ArtifactType::Footer => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
238            ArtifactType::Watermark => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
239            ArtifactType::PageNumber => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
240            ArtifactType::LineNumber => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
241            ArtifactType::Redaction => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
242            ArtifactType::Bates => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
243            ArtifactType::PaginationOther => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Pagination),
244            ArtifactType::Layout => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Layout),
245            ArtifactType::Page => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Page),
246            ArtifactType::Background => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactType::Background),
247            ArtifactType::Other => None,
248        }
249    }
250
251    pub(crate) fn to_pdf_artifact_subtype(self) -> Option<pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype<'static>> {
252        match self {
253            ArtifactType::Header => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::Header),
254            ArtifactType::Footer => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::Footer),
255            ArtifactType::Watermark => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::Watermark),
256            ArtifactType::PageNumber => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::PageNumber),
257            ArtifactType::LineNumber => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::LineNumber),
258            ArtifactType::Redaction => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::Redaction),
259            ArtifactType::Bates => Some(pdf_writer::types::ArtifactSubtype::Bates),
260            _ => None,
261        }
262    }
263}

265/// A language identifier as specified in RFC 3066. It will not be validated, so
266/// it's on the user of the library to ensure the tag is valid.
267pub type Lang<'a> = &'a str;
268/// An alternate text that describes some element in natural language.
269pub type Alt<'a> = &'a str;
270/// The actual intended textual content of a span. For example,
271/// if you have a hyphenated word, you can use `ActualText` to describe
272/// the same word without hyphens.
273pub type ActualText<'a> = &'a str;
274/// The expanded form of an abbreviation.
275pub type Expanded<'a> = &'a str;
276
277/// A content tag associated with the content it wraps.
278#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
279pub enum ContentTag<'a> {
280    /// Artifacts represent pieces of content that are not really part of the logical structure
281    /// of a document and should be excluded in the logical tree. These include for example headers,
282    /// footers, page background and similar.
283    Artifact(Artifact),
284    /// A content tag that wraps some text with specific properties.
285    ///
286    /// Spans should not be too long. At most, they should contain a single line of text, but they
287    /// can obviously be shorter, if text within a single line contains text with different styles
288    /// or different languages.
289    Span(SpanTag<'a>),
290    /// Use this tag for anything else that does not semantically fit into `Span` or `Artifact`.
291    /// This includes for example arbitrary paths, images or a mix of different content that cannot
292    /// be split up more.
293    Other,
294}
295
296impl ContentTag<'_> {
297    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Name<'static> {
298        match self {
299            ContentTag::Artifact(_) => Name(b"Artifact"),
300            ContentTag::Span(_) => Name(b"Span"),
301            ContentTag::Other => Name(b"P"),
302        }
303    }
304
305    pub(crate) fn write_properties(&self, sc: &mut SerializeContext, mut properties: PropertyList, page_height: f32) {
306        match self {
307            ContentTag::Artifact(artifact) => {
308                let at = artifact.kind.map_pdf_version(sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version());
309                let mut artifact_props = properties.artifact();
310
311                if let Some(bbox) = artifact.bbox {
312                    let transform = page_root_transform(page_height);
313                    let actual_rect = bbox.transform(transform).unwrap();
314                    artifact_props.bounding_box(actual_rect.to_pdf_rect());
315                }
316
317                if sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version() >= PdfVersion::Pdf17 {
318                    if at == ArtifactType::Header {
319                        artifact_props.attached([pdf_writer::types::ArtifactAttachment::Top]);
320                    }
321
322                    if at == ArtifactType::Footer {
323                        artifact_props.attached([pdf_writer::types::ArtifactAttachment::Bottom]);
324                    }
325
326                    if let Some(subtype) = at.to_pdf_artifact_subtype() {
327                        artifact_props.subtype(subtype);
328                    }
329                }
330
331                if let Some(artifact_type) = at.to_pdf_artifact_type() {
332                    artifact_props.kind(artifact_type);
333                }
334            }
335            ContentTag::Span(SpanTag { lang, alt_text, expanded, actual_text }) => {
336                if let Some(lang) = lang {
337                    properties.pair(Name(b"Lang"), TextStr(lang));
338                }
339
340                if let Some(alt) = alt_text {
341                    if sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version() >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
342                        properties.pair(Name(b"Alt"), TextStr(alt));
343                    }
344                }
345
346                if let Some(exp) = expanded {
347                    properties.pair(Name(b"E"), TextStr(exp));
348                }
349
350                if let Some(actual) = actual_text {
351                    if sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version() >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
352                        properties.actual_text(TextStr(actual));
353                    }
354                }
355            }
356            ContentTag::Other => {}
357        }
358    }
359}

361/// A span tag.
362#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
363pub struct SpanTag<'a> {
364    /// The language of the text.
365    pub lang: Option<Lang<'a>>,
366    /// An optional alternate text that describes the text (for example, if the text consists
367    /// of a star symbol, the alt text should describe that in natural language).
368    pub alt_text: Option<Alt<'a>>,
369    /// If the content of the span is an abbreviation, the expanded form of the
370    /// abbreviation should be provided here.
371    pub expanded: Option<Expanded<'a>>,
372    /// The actual text represented by the glyphs, i.e. if you have a hyphenated span
373    /// `row-`, then you can wrap it in an `ActualText` to remove the hyphenation
374    /// when copy-pasting.
375    pub actual_text: Option<ActualText<'a>>,
376}
377
378impl<'a> SpanTag<'a> {
379    /// An empty span tag.
380    pub fn empty() -> Self {
381        Self { lang: None, alt_text: None, expanded: None, actual_text: None }
382    }
383
384    /// Sets [`SpanTag::lang`].
385    pub fn with_lang(mut self, lang: Option<&'a str>) -> Self {
386        self.lang = lang;
387        self
388    }
389
390    /// Sets [`SpanTag::alt_text`].
391    pub fn with_alt_text(mut self, alt_text: Option<&'a str>) -> Self {
392        self.alt_text = alt_text;
393        self
394    }
395
396    /// Sets [`SpanTag::expanded`].
397    pub fn with_expanded(mut self, expanded: Option<&'a str>) -> Self {
398        self.expanded = expanded;
399        self
400    }
401
402    /// Sets [`SpanTag::actual_text`].
403    pub fn with_actual_text(mut self, actual_text: Option<&'a str>) -> Self {
404        self.actual_text = actual_text;
405        self
406    }
407}

410pub(crate) struct PageTagIdentifier {
411    pub(crate) page_index: usize,
412    pub(crate) mcid: i32,
413}
414
415impl From<PageTagIdentifier> for IdentifierType {
416    fn from(value: PageTagIdentifier) -> Self {
417        IdentifierType::PageIdentifier(value)
418    }
419}
420
421impl From<PageTagIdentifier> for Identifier {
422    fn from(value: PageTagIdentifier) -> Self {
423        Identifier(IdentifierInner::Real(value.into()))
424    }
425}
426
427impl PageTagIdentifier {
428    pub(crate) fn new(page_index: usize, mcid: i32) -> Self {
429        Self { page_index, mcid }
430    }
431
432    pub(crate) fn bump(&mut self) -> PageTagIdentifier {
433        let old = *self;
434
435        self.mcid = self.mcid.checked_add(1).unwrap();
436
437        old
438    }
439}

493impl TagKind {
494    pub(crate) fn write_kind(&self, struct_elem: &mut StructElement, sc: &mut SerializeContext) {
495        let pdf_version = sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version();
496        if pdf_version < self.minimum_version() {
497            // Fall back to P in case the tag is not supported with the current
498            // PDF version
499            struct_elem.kind(StructRole::P);
500            return;
501        }
502
503        match self {
504            Self::Part(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Part),
505            Self::Article(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::Art),
506            Self::Section(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Sect),
507            Self::Div(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Div),
508            Self::BlockQuote(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::BlockQuote),
509            Self::Caption(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Caption),
510            Self::TOC(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::TOC),
511            Self::TOCI(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::TOCI),
512            Self::Index(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::Index),
513            Self::P(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::P),
514            Self::L(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::L),
515            Self::LI(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::LI),
516            Self::Lbl(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Lbl),
517            Self::LBody(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::LBody),
518            Self::Table(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Table),
519            Self::TR(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::TR),
520            Self::TH(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::TH),
521            Self::TD(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::TD),
522            Self::THead(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::THead),
523            Self::TBody(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::TBody),
524            Self::TFoot(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::TFoot),
525            Self::Span(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Span),
526            Self::InlineQuote(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::Quote),
527            Self::Note(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::Note),
528            Self::Reference(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::Reference),
529            Self::BibEntry(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::BibEntry),
530            Self::Code(_) => write_kind_1_7(struct_elem, StructRole::Code),
531            Self::Link(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Link),
532            Self::Annot(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Annot),
533            Self::Figure(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Figure),
534            Self::Formula(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Formula),
535            Self::Form(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::Form),
536            Self::NonStruct(_) => write_kind_compat(sc, struct_elem, StructRole2::NonStruct),
537            // Custom structure roles that are registered in the `RoleMap`.
538            Self::Datetime(_) => write_kind_custom(sc, struct_elem, Name(b"Datetime")),
539            Self::Terms(_) => write_kind_custom(sc, struct_elem, Name(b"Terms")),
540            Self::Title(_) => write_kind_custom(sc, struct_elem, Name(b"Title")),
541            // PDF 2.0 structure roles that are conditionally registered.
542            Self::Hn(tag) => {
543                let role2 = StructRole2::Heading(tag.level());
544                if pdf_version < PdfVersion::Pdf20 {
545                    // Dynamically register custom headings `Hn` if the level
546                    // (`n >= 7`) isn't supported by PDF 1.7 and below.
547                    let compat = role2.compatibility_1_7(RoleMapOpts::default());
548                    if compat.into_pdf_1_7().is_none() {
549                        sc.global_objects.custom_heading_roles.insert(tag.level());
550                    }
551                    struct_elem.custom_kind(role2.to_name(&mut [0; 6]));
552                } else {
553                    struct_elem.kind_2(role2, sc.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref);
554                }
555            }
556            Self::Strong(_) => {
557                if pdf_version < PdfVersion::Pdf20 {
558                    struct_elem.custom_kind(Name(b"Strong"));
559                } else {
560                    struct_elem.kind_2(StructRole2::Strong, sc.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref);
561                }
562            }
563            Self::Em(_) => {
564                if pdf_version < PdfVersion::Pdf20 {
565                    struct_elem.custom_kind(Name(b"Em"));
566                } else {
567                    struct_elem.kind_2(StructRole2::Em, sc.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref);
568                }
569            }
570        };
571    }
572
573    pub(crate) fn minimum_version(&self) -> PdfVersion {
574        match self {
575            Self::Part(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
576            Self::Article(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
577            Self::Section(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
578            Self::Div(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
579            Self::BlockQuote(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
580            Self::Caption(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
581            Self::TOC(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
582            Self::TOCI(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
583            Self::Index(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
584            Self::P(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
585            Self::Hn(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
586            Self::L(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
587            Self::LI(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
588            Self::Lbl(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
589            Self::LBody(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
590            Self::Table(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
591            Self::TR(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
592            Self::TH(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
593            Self::TD(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
594            // TODO: writing `P` tags in PDF 1.4 will break the table structure.
595            // Instead consider just transparently inserting all children, which
596            // should be `TR`s anyway.
597            Self::THead(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf15,
598            Self::TBody(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf15,
599            Self::TFoot(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf15,
600            Self::Span(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
601            Self::InlineQuote(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
602            Self::Note(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
603            Self::Reference(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
604            Self::BibEntry(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
605            Self::Code(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
606            Self::Link(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
607            Self::Annot(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf15,
608            Self::Figure(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
609            Self::Formula(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
610            Self::Form(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
611            Self::NonStruct(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
612            Self::Datetime(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
613            Self::Terms(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
614            Self::Title(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
615            Self::Strong(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
616            Self::Em(_) => PdfVersion::Pdf14,
617        }
618    }
619
620    pub(crate) fn should_have_alt(&self) -> bool {
621        matches!(self, TagKind::Figure(_) | TagKind::Formula(_))
622    }
623
624    pub(crate) fn can_have_title(&self) -> bool {
625        matches!(self, Self::Hn(_))
626    }
627}
628
629fn write_kind_1_7(struct_elem: &mut StructElement, role: StructRole) {
630    struct_elem.kind(role);
631}
632
633/// If serializing a PDF 2.0 document, write a PDF 2.0 structure role, otherwise
634/// fall back to the compatible PDF 1.7 role.
635fn write_kind_compat(sc: &mut SerializeContext, struct_elem: &mut StructElement, role: StructRole2) {
636    if sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version() < PdfVersion::Pdf20 {
637        let compat = role.compatibility_1_7(RoleMapOpts::default());
638        struct_elem.kind(compat.role());
639    } else {
640        struct_elem.kind_2(role, sc.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref);
641    }
642}
643
644/// Write a custom role-mapped structure role. If serializing a PDF 2.0 document
645/// also write the custom krilla namespace.
646fn write_kind_custom(sc: &mut SerializeContext, struct_elem: &mut StructElement, name: Name) {
647    struct_elem.custom_kind(name);
648    if sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version() >= PdfVersion::Pdf20 {
649        struct_elem.namespace(sc.pdf2_ns.krilla_ref);
650    }
651}

653/// A node in a tag tree.
654#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
655pub enum Node {
656    /// A group node.
657    Group(TagGroup),
658    /// A leaf node.
659    Leaf(Identifier),
660}
661
662impl Node {
663    pub(crate) fn serialize(
664        &self,
665        sc: &mut SerializeContext,
666        parent_tree_map: &mut HashMap<IdentifierType, Ref>,
667        id_tree: &mut BTreeMap<TagId, Ref>,
668        parent: Ref,
669        note_id: &mut u32,
670        struct_elems: &mut Chunk,
671    ) -> KrillaResult<Option<Reference>> {
672        match self {
673            Node::Group(g) => Ok(Some(g.serialize(sc, parent_tree_map, id_tree, parent, note_id, struct_elems)?)),
674            Node::Leaf(ci) => match ci.0 {
675                IdentifierInner::Real(rci) => Ok(Some(Reference::ContentIdentifier(rci))),
676                IdentifierInner::Dummy => Ok(None),
677            },
678        }
679    }
680}
681
682impl From<TagGroup> for Node {
683    fn from(value: TagGroup) -> Self {
684        Node::Group(value)
685    }
686}
687
688impl From<Identifier> for Node {
689    fn from(value: Identifier) -> Self {
690        Node::Leaf(value)
691    }
692}

694#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
695pub(crate) enum Reference {
696    Ref(Ref),
697    ContentIdentifier(IdentifierType),
698}
699
700/// A tag group.
701#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
702pub struct TagGroup {
703    /// The tag of the tag group.
704    pub tag: TagKind,
705    /// The children of the tag group.
706    pub children: Vec<Node>,
707}
708
709impl TagGroup {
710    /// Create a new tag group with a specific tag.
711    pub fn new(tag: impl Into<TagKind>) -> Self {
712        Self { tag: tag.into(), children: vec![] }
713    }
714
715    /// Create a new tag group with a specific tag and a list of children.
716    pub fn with_children(tag: impl Into<TagKind>, children: Vec<Node>) -> Self {
717        Self { tag: tag.into(), children }
718    }
719
720    /// Append a new child to the tag group.
721    pub fn push(&mut self, child: impl Into<Node>) {
722        self.children.push(child.into())
723    }
724
725    pub(crate) fn serialize(
726        &self,
727        sc: &mut SerializeContext,
728        parent_tree_map: &mut HashMap<IdentifierType, Ref>,
729        id_tree: &mut BTreeMap<TagId, Ref>,
730        parent_ref: Ref,
731        note_id: &mut u32,
732        struct_elems: &mut Chunk,
733    ) -> KrillaResult<Reference> {
734        let elem_ref = sc.new_ref();
735        let mut children_refs = vec![];
736
737        for child in &self.children {
738            let serialized = child.serialize(sc, parent_tree_map, id_tree, elem_ref, note_id, struct_elems)?;
739            if let Some(ref_) = serialized {
740                children_refs.push(ref_);
741            }
742        }
743
744        let mut struct_elem = struct_elems.struct_element(elem_ref);
745        self.tag.write_kind(&mut struct_elem, sc);
746        struct_elem.parent(parent_ref);
747
748        let tag = self.tag.as_any();
749        let pdf_version = sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version();
750
751        if let Some(id) = tag.id() {
752            match id_tree.entry(id.clone()) {
753                Entry::Vacant(vacant) => {
754                    struct_elem.id(Str(id.as_bytes()));
755                    vacant.insert(elem_ref);
756                }
757                Entry::Occupied(_) => {
758                    return Err(KrillaError::DuplicateTagId(id.clone(), tag.location));
759                }
760            }
761        } else if matches!(self.tag, TagKind::Note(_)) {
762            // Explicitly don't use `TagId::from_bytes` to disambiguate note IDs
763            // from user provided IDs.
764            let mut id = TagId(SmallVec::new());
765            _ = write!(&mut id.0, "Note {note_id}");
766            struct_elem.id(Str(id.as_bytes()));
767            id_tree.insert(id, elem_ref);
768
769            *note_id += 1;
770        }
771
772        if self.tag.can_have_title() && tag.title().is_none_or(str::is_empty) {
773            sc.register_validation_error(ValidationError::MissingHeadingTitle);
774        }
775
776        if self.tag.should_have_alt() && tag.alt_text().is_none_or(str::is_empty) {
777            sc.register_validation_error(ValidationError::MissingAltText(tag.location));
778        }
779
780        // TODO: Once we have a generalized mechanism for validating tag trees,
781        // validate TH-outside-THead structure for PDF < 1.5.
782
783        for attr in tag.attrs.iter() {
784            let Attr::Struct(attr) = attr else {
785                continue;
786            };
787            match attr {
788                StructAttr::Id(_) => (), // Handled above
789                StructAttr::Title(title) => {
790                    struct_elem.title(TextStr(title));
791                }
792                StructAttr::Lang(lang) => {
793                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf14 {
794                        struct_elem.lang(TextStr(lang));
795                    }
796                }
797                StructAttr::AltText(alt) => {
798                    struct_elem.alt(TextStr(alt));
799                }
800                StructAttr::Expanded(expanded) => {
801                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
802                        struct_elem.expanded(TextStr(expanded));
803                    }
804                }
805                StructAttr::ActualText(actual_text) => {
806                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf14 {
807                        struct_elem.actual_text(TextStr(actual_text));
808                    }
809                }
810
811                // Not really an attribute
812                StructAttr::HeadingLevel(_) => (),
813            }
814        }
815
816        let mut attributes = LazyCell::new(|| struct_elem.attributes());
817
818        // Lazily initialize the list attributes to avoid an empty array.
819        let mut list_attributes = LazyCell::new(|| attributes.push().list());
820        for attr in tag.attrs.iter() {
821            let Attr::List(attr) = attr else {
822                continue;
823            };
824            match attr {
825                ListAttr::Numbering(numbering) => {
826                    list_attributes.list_numbering(numbering.to_pdf());
827                }
828            }
829        }
830        list_attributes.finish();
831
832        // Lazily initialize the table attributes to avoid an empty array.
833        let mut table_attributes = LazyCell::new(|| attributes.push().table());
834        for attr in tag.attrs.iter() {
835            let Attr::Table(attr) = attr else {
836                continue;
837            };
838            match attr {
839                TableAttr::Summary(summary) => {
840                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf17 {
841                        table_attributes.summary(TextStr(summary));
842                    }
843                }
844                TableAttr::HeaderScope(scope) => {
845                    if pdf_version >= VersionedFeature::TableHeaderScope.minimum_pdf_version() {
846                        table_attributes.scope(scope.to_pdf());
847                    } else if scope == &TableHeaderScope::Row {
848                        // Without `Scope`, the correct cell to point to is ambiguous.
849                        sc.register_validation_error(ValidationError::RequiresNewerPdfVersion(VersionedFeature::TableHeaderScope, tag.location));
850                    }
851                }
852                TableAttr::CellHeaders(headers) => {
853                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
854                        let id_strs = headers.iter().map(|id| Str(id.as_bytes()));
855                        table_attributes.headers().items(id_strs);
856                    }
857                }
858                TableAttr::RowSpan(n) => {
859                    table_attributes.row_span(n.get() as i32);
860                }
861                TableAttr::ColSpan(n) => {
862                    table_attributes.col_span(n.get() as i32);
863                }
864            }
865        }
866        table_attributes.finish();
867
868        // Lazily initialize the list attributes to avoid an empty array.
869        let mut layout_attributes = LazyCell::new(|| attributes.push().layout());
870        for attr in tag.attrs.iter() {
871            let Attr::Layout(attr) = attr else {
872                continue;
873            };
874            match attr {
875                LayoutAttr::Placement(placement) => {
876                    layout_attributes.placement(placement.to_pdf());
877                }
878                LayoutAttr::WritingMode(writing_mode) => {
879                    layout_attributes.writing_mode(writing_mode.to_pdf());
880                }
881                &LayoutAttr::BBox(BBox { page_idx, rect }) => {
882                    let Some(page_info) = sc.page_infos().get(page_idx) else {
883                        panic!(
884                            "tag tree contains bounding box with page index {page_idx}, \
885                            but document only has {} pages",
886                            sc.page_infos().len()
887                        );
888                    };
889                    let transform = page_root_transform(page_info.size().height());
890                    let actual_rect = rect.transform(transform).unwrap();
891                    layout_attributes.bbox(actual_rect.to_pdf_rect());
892                }
893                &LayoutAttr::Width(width) => {
894                    layout_attributes.width(width);
895                }
896                &LayoutAttr::Height(height) => {
897                    layout_attributes.height(height);
898                }
899                &LayoutAttr::BackgroundColor(color) => {
900                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
901                        layout_attributes.background_color(color.into());
902                    }
903                }
904                LayoutAttr::BorderColor(sides) => {
905                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
906                        let sides = sides.map_pdf(NaiveRgbColor::into_f32_array);
907                        layout_attributes.border_color(sides);
908                    }
909                }
910                LayoutAttr::BorderStyle(sides) => {
911                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
912                        let sides = sides.map_pdf(BorderStyle::to_pdf);
913                        layout_attributes.border_style(sides);
914                    }
915                }
916                LayoutAttr::BorderThickness(sides) => {
917                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
918                        layout_attributes.border_thickness(sides.into_pdf());
919                    }
920                }
921                LayoutAttr::Padding(sides) => {
922                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
923                        layout_attributes.padding(sides.into_pdf());
924                    }
925                }
926                &LayoutAttr::Color(color) => {
927                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
928                        layout_attributes.color(color.into());
929                    }
930                }
931                &LayoutAttr::SpaceBefore(margin) => {
932                    layout_attributes.space_before(margin);
933                }
934                &LayoutAttr::SpaceAfter(margin) => {
935                    layout_attributes.space_after(margin);
936                }
937                &LayoutAttr::StartIndent(margin) => {
938                    layout_attributes.start_indent(margin);
939                }
940                &LayoutAttr::EndIndent(margin) => {
941                    layout_attributes.end_indent(margin);
942                }
943                &LayoutAttr::TextIndent(indent) => {
944                    layout_attributes.text_indent(indent);
945                }
946                LayoutAttr::BlockAlign(alignment) => {
947                    layout_attributes.block_align(alignment.to_pdf());
948                }
949                LayoutAttr::InlineAlign(alignment) => {
950                    layout_attributes.inline_align(alignment.to_pdf());
951                }
952                LayoutAttr::TextAlign(alignment) => {
953                    layout_attributes.text_align(alignment.to_pdf());
954                }
955                LayoutAttr::TableBorderStyle(sides) => {
956                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
957                        let sides = sides.map_pdf(BorderStyle::to_pdf);
958                        layout_attributes.table_border_style(sides);
959                    }
960                }
961                LayoutAttr::TablePadding(sides) => {
962                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
963                        layout_attributes.table_padding(sides.into_pdf());
964                    }
965                }
966                &LayoutAttr::BaselineShift(shift) => {
967                    layout_attributes.baseline_shift(shift);
968                }
969                LayoutAttr::LineHeight(height) => {
970                    layout_attributes.line_height(height.to_pdf());
971                }
972                &LayoutAttr::TextDecorationColor(color) => {
973                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
974                        layout_attributes.text_decoration_color(color.into());
975                    }
976                }
977                &LayoutAttr::TextDecorationThickness(thickness) => {
978                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
979                        layout_attributes.text_decoration_thickness(thickness);
980                    }
981                }
982                LayoutAttr::TextDecorationType(style) => {
983                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
984                        layout_attributes.text_decoration_type(style.to_pdf());
985                    }
986                }
987                &LayoutAttr::GlyphOrientationVertical(orientation) => {
988                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf15 {
989                        layout_attributes.glyph_orientation_vertical(orientation.to_pdf());
990                    }
991                }
992                LayoutAttr::ColumnCount(columns) => {
993                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf16 {
994                        layout_attributes.column_count(columns.get() as i32);
995                    }
996                }
997                LayoutAttr::ColumnGap(gap) => {
998                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf16 {
999                        let sizes = layout_attributes.column_gap();
1000                        match gap {
1001                            ColumnDimensions::All(gap) => sizes.uniform(*gap),
1002                            ColumnDimensions::Specific(values) => {
1003                                sizes.individual().items(values.iter().copied());
1004                            }
1005                        }
1006                    }
1007                }
1008                LayoutAttr::ColumnWidths(width) => {
1009                    if pdf_version >= PdfVersion::Pdf16 {
1010                        let sizes = layout_attributes.column_widths();
1011                        match width {
1012                            ColumnDimensions::All(width) => sizes.uniform(*width),
1013                            ColumnDimensions::Specific(values) => {
1014                                sizes.individual().items(values.iter().copied());
1015                            }
1016                        }
1017                    }
1018                }
1019            }
1020        }
1021        layout_attributes.finish();
1022
1023        attributes.finish();
1024
1025        serialize_children(sc, elem_ref, children_refs, parent_tree_map, &mut struct_elem)?;
1026        struct_elem.finish();
1027
1028        Ok(Reference::Ref(elem_ref))
1029    }
1030
1031    fn validate(&self, id_tree: &BTreeMap<TagId, Ref>) -> KrillaResult<()> {
1032        if let Some(headers) = self.tag.headers() {
1033            for id in headers.iter() {
1034                if !id_tree.contains_key(id) {
1035                    return Err(KrillaError::UnknownTagId(id.clone(), self.tag.location()));
1036                }
1037            }
1038        }
1039
1040        for child in self.children.iter() {
1041            if let Node::Group(group) = child {
1042                group.validate(id_tree)?;
1043            }
1044        }
1045        Ok(())
1046    }
1047}
1048
1049/// A tag tree.
1050#[derive(Default)]
1051pub struct TagTree {
1052    /// The children of the tag tree.
1053    pub children: Vec<Node>,
1054    /// Language attribute for the auto-generated Document root structure element.
1055    pub lang: Option<String>,
1056}
1057
1058impl From<Vec<Node>> for TagTree {
1059    fn from(children: Vec<Node>) -> Self {
1060        Self { children, lang: None }
1061    }
1062}
1063
1064impl TagTree {
1065    /// Create a new tag tree.
1066    pub fn new() -> Self {
1067        Self { children: vec![], lang: None }
1068    }
1069
1070    /// Set the language attribute on the Document root structure element.
1071    ///
1072    /// This sets `/Lang` on the auto-generated Document structure element,
1073    /// which is distinct from the catalog-level `/Lang` set via
1074    /// [`Metadata::language`](crate::third_party::krilla::metadata::Metadata::language).
1075    pub fn with_lang(mut self, lang: Option<String>) -> Self {
1076        self.lang = lang;
1077        self
1078    }
1079
1080    /// Append a new child to the tag tree.
1081    pub fn push(&mut self, child: impl Into<Node>) {
1082        self.children.push(child.into())
1083    }
1084
1085    pub(crate) fn serialize(
1086        &self,
1087        sc: &mut SerializeContext,
1088        chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer,
1089        parent_tree_map: &mut HashMap<IdentifierType, Ref>,
1090        id_tree_map: &mut BTreeMap<TagId, Ref>,
1091        struct_tree_ref: Ref,
1092    ) -> KrillaResult<Ref> {
1093        let root_ref = sc.new_ref();
1094        let mut struct_elems = sc.new_chunk();
1095
1096        // Keeps track of the ID of notes in the IDTree. We currently only write IDs for notes,
1097        // which is why we use this simple variable, but this should be refactored if we write
1098        // the IDs for multiple types of struct elements in the future.
1099        let mut note_id = 1;
1100
1101        let mut children_refs = vec![];
1102
1103        for child in &self.children {
1104            let serialized = child.serialize(sc, parent_tree_map, id_tree_map, root_ref, &mut note_id, &mut struct_elems)?;
1105
1106            if let Some(ref_) = serialized {
1107                children_refs.push(ref_);
1108            }
1109        }
1110
1111        let mut struct_elem = struct_elems.indirect(root_ref).start::<StructElement>();
1112        struct_elem.kind(StructRole::Document);
1113        struct_elem.parent(struct_tree_ref);
1114        if let Some(lang) = &self.lang {
1115            if sc.serialize_settings().pdf_version() >= PdfVersion::Pdf14 {
1116                struct_elem.lang(TextStr(lang));
1117            }
1118        }
1119        serialize_children(sc, root_ref, children_refs, parent_tree_map, &mut struct_elem)?;
1120
1121        struct_elem.finish();
1122        chunk_container.non_stream.struct_elements = Some(struct_elems);
1123
1124        Ok(root_ref)
1125    }
1126
1127    pub(crate) fn validate(&self, id_tree: &BTreeMap<TagId, Ref>) -> KrillaResult<()> {
1128        for child in self.children.iter() {
1129            if let Node::Group(group) = child {
1130                group.validate(id_tree)?;
1131            }
1132        }
1133        Ok(())
1134    }
1135}
1136
1137fn serialize_children(
1138    sc: &mut SerializeContext,
1139    parent_ref: Ref,
1140    children_refs: Vec<Reference>,
1141    parent_tree_map: &mut HashMap<IdentifierType, Ref>,
1142    struct_elem: &mut StructElement,
1143) -> KrillaResult<()> {
1144    // We can define a /Pg element on the struct element. If a marked content reference
1145    // is part of the same page as that entry, we can just write the mcid, otherwise, we
1146    // need to write a full marked content reference.
1147    // In our case, we just use the first marked content reference we can find as the
1148    // entry in the /Pg dict.
1149    let mut struct_page_ref = None;
1150    let mut struct_children = struct_elem.children();
1151
1152    for child in children_refs {
1153        match child {
1154            Reference::Ref(r) => {
1155                struct_children.struct_element(r);
1156            }
1157            Reference::ContentIdentifier(it) => match it {
1158                IdentifierType::PageIdentifier(pi) => {
1159                    let page_ref = sc
1160                        .page_infos()
1161                        .get(pi.page_index)
1162                        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
1163                            panic!(
1164                                "tag tree contains identifier from page {}, but document only has {} pages",
1165                                pi.page_index + 1,
1166                                sc.page_infos().len()
1167                            )
1168                        })
1169                        .ref_();
1170
1171                    if struct_page_ref.is_none() {
1172                        struct_page_ref = Some(page_ref);
1173                    }
1174
1175                    if parent_tree_map.contains_key(&pi.into()) {
1176                        panic!("the identifier {pi:?} appears twice in the tag tree");
1177                    }
1178
1179                    parent_tree_map.insert(pi.into(), parent_ref);
1180
1181                    if struct_page_ref == Some(page_ref) {
1182                        struct_children.marked_content_id(pi.mcid);
1183                    } else {
1184                        struct_children.marked_content_ref().marked_content_id(pi.mcid).page(page_ref);
1185                    }
1186                }
1187                IdentifierType::AnnotationIdentifier(ai) => {
1188                    let Some(page_info) = sc.page_infos_mut().get_mut(ai.page_index) else {
1189                        panic!("tag tree contains identifier from page {}, but document only has {} pages", ai.page_index + 1, sc.page_infos().len());
1190                    };
1191
1192                    let page_ref = page_info.ref_();
1193                    let Some((annotation_ref, struct_parent)) = page_info.annotations_mut().get_mut(ai.annot_index) else {
1194                        panic!(
1195                            "tag tree contains identifier from annotation {} on page {}, but page only has {} annotations",
1196                            ai.annot_index + 1,
1197                            ai.page_index + 1,
1198                            page_info.annotations().len()
1199                        );
1200                    };
1201
1202                    if parent_tree_map.contains_key(&ai.into()) {
1203                        panic!("identifier {ai:?} appears twice in the tag tree");
1204                    }
1205                    parent_tree_map.insert(ai.into(), *annotation_ref);
1206
1207                    struct_parent.set(parent_ref).expect("only one parent");
1208
1209                    struct_children.object_ref().page(page_ref).object(*annotation_ref);
1210                }
1211            },
1212        }
1213    }
1214    struct_children.finish();
1215
1216    if let Some(spr) = struct_page_ref {
1217        struct_elem.page(spr);
1218    }
1219
1220    Ok(())
1221}
1222
1223/// Where a layout artifact is attached to the page edge.
1224#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
1225#[allow(missing_docs)]
1226pub enum ArtifactAttachment {
1227    Left,
1228    Top,
1229    Right,
1230    Bottom,
1231}
